name: Fall of Constantinople

phases.title: The armies take their positions
phases.text: The Ottoman army camped outside the land walls. The European regulars lay along the walls, the troops from Anatolia south of the Lycus, and the guns and Janissaries near the Mesoteichion. Constantine held the Mesoteichion and Giustiniani the Charisian Gate to the north.

phases.title: The guns open fire and the chain holds the fleet out
phases.text: Mehmed's cannons fired on the walls for weeks, but the Byzantines repaired most of the damage after each shot. The Ottoman fleet made probing attacks but could not enter the Golden Horn because of the chain.

phases.title: Ships are hauled over the hill into the Horn
phases.text: Mehmed had a road of greased logs laid across Galata and dragged his ships over the hill into the Golden Horn, bypassing the chain. This threatened the supply ships from Pera and demoralised the defenders.

phases.title: The fire-ship attack on the hauled ships fails
phases.text: The defenders tried to destroy the Ottoman ships in the Golden Horn with fire ships. The Ottomans forced the Christians to retreat with many casualties.

phases.title: The Ottoman first waves attack at Blachernae
phases.text: The Christian troops of the Ottoman Empire attacked first, followed by waves of irregular azaps and Anatolian Turkmen. They focused on a damaged section of the Blachernae walls in the north-west part of the city.

phases.title: The Turkmen breach the wall and are pushed back
phases.text: The Turkmen mercenaries breached this older, weaker section of the walls and entered the city, but the defenders pushed them back just as quickly.

phases.title: The Janissaries attack and Giustiniani is wounded
phases.text: The last wave, the elite Janissaries, attacked the city walls. Giustiniani, the Genoese general in charge of the defenders on land, was grievously wounded, and his evacuation from the ramparts caused a panic in the ranks of the defenders.

phases.title: The Genoese retreat and Constantine holds
phases.text: Giustiniani's Genoese troops retreated into the city and towards the harbour. Constantine and his men, left to their own devices, continued to hold their ground against the Janissaries.

phases.title: The defenders are overwhelmed and the Venetians fall back
phases.text: Constantine's men could not prevent the Ottomans from entering the city, and the defenders were overwhelmed at several points along the wall. Janissaries pressed forward, many Greek soldiers ran back home, and the Venetians retreated to their ships.

phases.title: The Venetians leave and the Ottoman navy holds the Horn
phases.text: The Venetian captain had the gate of the Golden Horn broken open, and the Venetians left in ships filled with soldiers and refugees. A few Genoese ships and the Emperor's ships followed them. The Ottoman navy took control of the Golden Horn by midday.

note: This plan shows the whole siege, not a single field: the land walls face west, the Golden Horn lies to the north and the Sea of Marmara to the south. The accounts place the Ottoman troops by their position along the walls and the defenders by sector, so the blocks stand in those places only roughly. Giustiniani is drawn at his first post, the Charisian Gate; the accounts say he was later shifted to the Mesoteichion but not when. Zagan Pasha's troops north of the Horn, the Ottoman mining of mid-May, the Byzantine reserves, the four Christian ships that entered the Horn on 20 April and the sectors of the sea walls are not drawn. Where the Ottoman ships stood outside the chain is a judgement; the accounts do not say. They also give another account of the end of Constantine, so his fate is not drawn.
